answer: The nectar multiplier is published, charged in falcon, and meadow lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3579 identities would post 2343 proofs and burn roughly 38 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
